model: Insurer FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Cyber-breach litigation and OAIC civil penalty, probability-weighted post-tax cost
equity_bridge.note: OAIC Federal Court civil penalty proceedings plus the customer class action (leave to appeal the Deloitte-report discovery ruling refused March 2026) are unprovided; cumulative breach costs already >$125m. Expected value of a penalty plus settlement ~150m (penalties are not tax-deductible); bear narrative carries a larger outcome inside its margin path. Not in the equity_bridge per scenario because the bridge is global.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (5.0%), cross-checked against revenue 5yr CAGR 5.7% and the post-AASB17 underlying NPAT CAGR of 5.7% (FY24 570.4 -> FY26 636.8); base year-1 growth of 5.5% sits between them
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (7.6-7.7%) exceed the equity CAGR (5.0%) by more than 30% in relative terms. Not a red flag here: the gap is the 80%+ payout ratio (retained earnings are a small share of NPAT), not accounting. The 3-year figures straddle the AASB 17 adoption (FY23 as originally reported 511.1 NPAT / 18.6c EPS; restated under AASB 17 to 308.6) and the FY25 COVID-reserve finalisation (-128.0 after tax), so the 3-year EPS and FCF CAGRs are on a mixed basis and are only indicative.
historical_growth.notes: The 'FCF' CAGRs are computed on NPAT attributable to shareholders (FY21 441.2 -> FY26 638.7; FY23 511.1 -> FY26 638.7), because reported FCF for a health insurer is timing noise (see inputs.notes). SBC is 0.1% of revenue so an SBC-adjusted series is indistinguishable from the reported one. Reported FCF series: FY21 447.1, FY22 913.4, FY23 142.6, FY24 810.9, FY25 311.1, FY26 420.5 -- no CAGR on that series means anything.

scenario_narratives.base: Medibank remains a regulated, slow-compounding cash payer. Revenue grows ~5.5% in FY27 (premium rate, small volume gain, Revenue Mix drag, Health +25%) and decays to 3% by FY36. Resident insurance margin is held flat at FY26 levels as management guides, with the FY26 COVID utilisation benefit unwinding offset by the 4.41% April-2026 premium increase; Medibank Health scales toward its FY30 $200m segment profit target and lifts group margin ~0.15pp; cybercrime costs fade from $35m to under $20m and then out. About 89% of NPAT is distributable once the Health build-out is funded; the ~$3.4bn regulated portfolio and its ~$180m investment income stay inside the business. A probability-weighted $150m post-tax cost for the OAIC penalty and class action is deducted in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: The health-company pivot works: Health exceeds $200m of segment profit by FY30, primary care/virtual care lower claims cost, market share recovers above 26.8%, the non-resident book rebounds on visa settings, and the expense ratio improves. Group margin expands ~1pp to 12.4% and growth holds ~5-6% for four years with 3.5% terminal growth. Cyber litigation settles within the bridge amount.
scenario_narratives.bear: The regulator becomes the margin-setter: the April 2027 approval lags the step-up in hospital claims growth, the COVID benefit unwinds uncompensated, downgrading widens and aggressive competitor/aggregator tactics lift acquisition cost, so group margin falls to ~10.3% before a slow partial recovery. Cybercrime costs stay ~$35m and the OAIC penalty plus class action exceed the bridge. Growth slows to 3% and 2.5% terminal. The company stays profitable and dividend-paying throughout -- this is a margin story, not a solvency story.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Medibank is valued as an earnings-distribution stream at an 8.5% AUD cost of equity, not as a compounder of book value and not on reported free cash flow. The regulated investment portfolio is neither added as net cash nor stripped of its income. Value comes from ~89% of NPAT being paid out and growing at roughly health-cost inflation; the market price implies either a lower discount rate (Australian holders can use the franking credits, which this NZ-based model gives no value to) or margin expansion the guidance does not support.
key_risks_to_valuation: Annual government premium-rate approval lags claims inflation (FY27 hospital claims growth per unit guided to step up 2.1% -> 3.6%)
OAIC civil penalty and customer class action outcomes are unprovided and could exceed the $150m bridge
Revenue Mix / downgrading and aggregator competition compress acquisition economics
Medibank Health FY30 $200m target depends on Better Medical integration and further M&A
Net investment income (~$180m) falls ~$6.4m per 25bp RBA cut
Franking credits are excluded: an Australian tax-resident buyer's fair value is meaningfully higher than this model's

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.06-5.31
data_sources.financials: MPL.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics from FY2015-FY2026 annual reports and H1 FY2016-H1 FY2026 interim reports; FY2026 annual report group summary income statement (MPL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:1016-1064), segment note (4505-4554), underlying NPAT reconciliation (4876-4882), cash flow (4425-4464)
data_sources.qualitative: MPL.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-24), FY2026 annual report outlook section

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payment transactions' 11.4 (MPL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:4386); no separate equity-award tax line (awards settled by on-market purchase, 10.7m in FY26)
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,754.0m ordinary shares, unchanged since the 2014 IPO; performance rights are settled by on-market purchase (FY26 10.7m), so basic = diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks are the funding of the flat count and are value-neutral.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is FCFE (post-tax earnings attributable to shareholders less reinvestment). Built in AUD: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% (Sept 2026) + 0.75 beta x 5.5% AUD equity risk premium = 8.5%. Beta below market: community-rated, non-discretionary product with no catastrophe exposure and 10 years of positive earnings. Regulatory pricing risk, claims inflation and the cyber litigation are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not as a WACC premium (risk charged once). Same rate for all three scenarios. Cf. IAG.AX at 9.0% (general insurer with cat risk).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B: leases as an operating cost. Full FY26 lease cash (principal 41.2 + interest 12.3 = 53.5, 0.59% of revenue) is charged through lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (198.9 non-current + 39.1 current) are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (105.1 total less ~41.2 ROU = ~64, 0.70% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. FY26 NCI share of profit 7.6 (pre-tax ~10.9) is netted out of the EBITDA margin, so modelled FY0 NOPAT ties to NPAT attributable to Medibank shareholders (638.7); no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.net_cash_note: net_debt held at ZERO by design. Borrowings are 35.9 (immaterial). Cash & equivalents 570.4 and the ~$3.4bn investment portfolio back insurance contract liabilities and APRA regulatory capital (health insurance capital ratio 13.3% vs 10-12% target band, plus a $250m additional capital adequacy requirement imposed by APRA after the 2022 cyber event and still in place). None of it is distributable, so the matching-asset rule applies in reverse: the asset stays out of the bridge and its income (net investment income 178.9 in FY26) stays IN the flows. interest_income is therefore 0 in the owner-FCF identity.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Insurer FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine (same family as IAG.AX, GMG.AX, CHC.AX). The dcf-methods routing table defaults insurers to BVPS-compounding x exit P/B, but Medibank does not compound book: ROE ~26%, dividend payout 75-85% of underlying NPAT (83% in FY26), shareholders' equity has grown only ~5%/yr for a decade. The value is the earnings stream paid out, so it is capitalised at the cost of equity. The engine's 'EBITDA margin' is PBT attributable to shareholders + D&A ex-ROU + lease cash + SBC, all as % of group revenue from external customers (FY26: 11.47%); the engine then charges SBC and lease cost explicitly, deducts D&A, taxes EBIT at 30% (Australian statutory; FY26 effective 30.3%), adds back D&A and deducts 'capex', which here bundles (i) PPE + intangibles capex (FY26 91.1, 1.0% of revenue), (ii) bolt-on M&A capital for the Medibank Health build-out toward its FY30 target of ~$700m capital employed (Better Medical 163.5 in FY26; ~0.5% of revenue p.a. to FY30), and (iii) regulatory capital retained to hold the capital ratio as premiums grow (~0.4-0.5% of revenue). FY0 tie-out: NOPAT on these components = 639 vs reported attributable NPAT 638.7. Mature FCFE conversion ~89% of NPAT, consistent with g = ROE x retention (26% x 11.5% = 3%). Reported OCF/FCF are NOT used as the base: an insurer's OCF is dominated by the timing of premiums received in advance of the 1 April rate rise (H1 FY26 OCF -256.9, FY26 +511.6, FY24 +868.5); last_fcf is recorded for the identity only. Revenue base is group revenue from external customers (9,115.2), which includes health insurance revenue, Medibank Health revenue and is on the AASB 17 basis (FY24 onward). FY26 base is clean: statutory NPAT 638.7 vs underlying 636.8 (normalisation only -1.9 for investment returns; no COVID reserve movement). Franking credits are NOT valued: the house investor is NZ-resident and cannot use them; an Australian holder would add roughly 30/70 of the 4.2% dividend yield.
inputs.fy27_guidance_used: Resident gross margin broadly consistent with FY26 (contingent on April 2027 premium approval); hospital claims growth per policy unit steps up 2.1% -> ~3.6% as the $74.8m FY26 COVID utilisation benefit does not repeat, offset by the 4.41% April 2026 premium increase; Revenue Mix (downgrading) drag ~150bps again; Medibank Health segment profit +~25% (full year of Better Medical); cybercrime costs <$20m (FY26 34.9); net investment income to benefit from asset growth (~$6.4m per 25bp RBA move); expense ratio stable to modestly improving.

bear.rationale: April 2027 premium approval lands below claims inflation while the $74.8m COVID utilisation benefit unwinds uncompensated (~-0.8pp resident gross margin), aggregator-led competition lifts acquisition cost and downgrading, cybercrime costs persist at ~35m/yr and the OAIC penalty plus class action cost materially more than the 150m bridge (an extra ~-0.3pp of margin in FY27-FY28). Health bolt-ons continue at lower returns. Margin recovers only partially as later premium rounds catch up.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 5.5%: ~4.4% April-2026 premium rate (nine months of it in FY27) + ~1% resident policyholder growth - ~1.5% Revenue Mix drag + non-resident recovery + Medibank Health +25-30% (7% of revenue). Decays to 3.0% as premium approvals track health-cost inflation and Health matures.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 actual 11.47% (pre-SBC, pre-lease, attributable). FY27 11.45%: resident gross margin held per guidance (premium rise offsets the $74.8m COVID benefit unwinding), cybercrime costs fall 34.9 -> ~20 (+0.15pp), Health profit +25% (+0.25pp on group), offset by intensified Q4 FY26 competition and a step-up in hospital claims growth per unit that management only says is 'broadly' covered. Then +0.05pp/yr to 11.6% as Health (higher-growth) reaches its FY30 $200m segment profit target; no insurance margin expansion assumed. Implied FY27 NPAT ~675m (+5.7% on statutory 638.7, +6% on underlying 636.8).
base.capex_rationale: 2.0% of revenue through FY30 = 1.0% PPE/intangibles + ~0.5% Health bolt-on M&A + ~0.5% regulatory capital retained on 5% premium growth; steps to 1.6% once the Health build-out completes and growth slows toward 3%. Mature FCFE ~89% of NPAT, consistent with an 80-85% payout policy plus a small capital buffer.
base.wc_rationale: Zero. The float generated by premium growth sits in the regulated investment portfolio, which is treated as non-distributable (see net_cash_note); capturing it would contradict that.

bull.rationale: Market share regains >26.8% by FY28, non-resident book grows solidly, Medibank Health exceeds $200m segment profit by FY30 (+0.6pp group margin), expense ratio improves ~30bp, cyber costs end and the litigation settles inside the 150m bridge. Same 8.5% cost of equity: the upside lives in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25% because pricing power sits with a single regulator (annual premium approval) and there is live, unquantified Federal Court litigation from the 2022 breach; bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things at once (regulator generosity, Health hitting $200m by FY30, and margin expansion in a commoditised community-rated product). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
